extracted.intended_audience: International Searching Authority examiners (e.g., USPTO examiners) preparing PCT international search reports and written opinions
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and finalizing the Form PCT/ISA/210 International Search Report and Form PCT/ISA/237 Written Opinion, including what to record in each box, citation categories, abstract/title requirements, search history, and timing. Targeted at examiners acting as the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheets subject to international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Only the “second sheet”, the “continuation of second sheet” (if any), the “continuation of first sheet (2)” (if any), and the “extra sheet” (if any), as well as any separate sheet with information on members of patent families, will be the subject of international publication; the “first sheet,” “continuation of first sheet (1)” (if any), and the “continuation of first sheet (3)” (if any) contain only information which will already appear on the front page of the publication (PCT Rule 48.2(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the correct total number of sheets on the first sheet, counting only filled-in sheets from Form PCT/ISA/210 (do not count blank sheets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the International Search Report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report contains citations of documents considered to be relevant (PCT Rule 43.5 & Admin. Instr. Sec. 503), classification of the subject matter (PCT Rule 43.3 & Admin. Instr. Sec. 504), and an indication of the fields searched (PCT Rule 43.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations of particular relevance must be specially indicated (Admin. Instr. Sec. 505). Citations of certain special categories must be indicated (Sec. 507). Citations not relevant to all claims must be related to the specific claim numbers (Sec. 508). If only certain passages are relevant, identify page/column/lines (PCT Rule 43.5(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 1a — Basis of the report: language
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the search is carried out on the basis of the international application in the language filed or on the basis of a translation into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most circumstances check the first box (language as filed). If based on a translation into English, check the second box and indicate English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 1b — Rectification of an obvious mistake
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the application includes rectification of an obvious mistake authorized by or notified to the ISA under PCT Rule 91, box 1b is checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization/notification will typically be indicated on a Notification of Decision Concerning Request for Rectification (Form PCT/RO/109 or PCT/ISA/217).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 1c / Box No. I — Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application discloses nucleotide/amino acid sequences, box 1c is checked and Box No. I indicates whether the sequence listing was filed as part of the application or subsequent for the purpose of international search and whether accompanied by the required statement that it does not go beyond disclosure as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 2 indicates the report was established to the extent a meaningful search could be carried out without a WIPO ST.26-compliant sequence listing. Item 3 is for additional comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 2 / Box No. II — Limitation of the subject of the international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The report must indicate whether any claims are unsearchable for specified reasons and identify the claims and reasons when limitations are applied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three categories where such limitations may arise are: (A) claims not required to be searched by the ISA (see MPEP §1843.02); (B) claims where a meaningful search cannot be carried out (see MPEP §1843.03); (C) multiple dependent claims not complying with PCT Rule 6.4(a). If limitations applied, check Box 2 and complete Box No. II with details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 3 / Box No. III — Lack of unity of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lack of unity is found, box 3 is checked and Box No. III is completed to indicate separate inventions, whether additional search fees were requested/paid, which claims were searched, and whether any protest accompanied payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use items 1–4 under Box No. III to indicate: (1) all searchable claims covered because applicant paid all additional fees; (2) examiner did not invite additional fees and ISR covers all searchable claims; (3) applicant paid only some fees (indicate which claims covered); (4) no timely payment — ISR restricted to the invention first mentioned in the claims (indicate claims covered). Enter an explanation of separate inventions in the space provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remark on Protest boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: Three boxes indicate whether payment of additional search fees was accompanied by a protest, whether a protest fee is required, or payment was not accompanied by a protest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the first box if payment was accompanied by a protest. The second box is not checked for ISA/US since it does not require a protest fee. Check the third box if payment was not accompanied by a protest. See MPEP §1850 for protest procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 4 — Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention shall be short (preferably from two to seven words when in English or translated into English) and precise (PCT Rule 4.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use personal names, trade names, ‘etc.’ or vague single-word titles like “Method,” “Apparatus,” or “Chemical Compounds.” The examiner must draft a new title if missing or deficient and is not required to obtain the applicant’s approval of the new title. On the ISR first sheet indicate whether the title text is approved or has been established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 5 — Abstract contents and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must be a summary of the disclosure in the description, claims, and drawings; indicate the technical field, clearly state the technical problem, the gist of the solution, and principal uses; include applicable chemical formulae (PCT Rule 8.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should be as concise as disclosure permits (preferably 50–150 words in English). It must not contain statements on alleged merits or speculative applications. Each main technical feature mentioned and illustrated by a drawing should be followed by a reference sign in parentheses (PCT Rule 8.1(d)). On the ISR first sheet indicate approval of text or enter a newly established abstract and state the defect (e.g., too long, missing). Applicant may submit modifications within one month from mailing of the ISR (PCT Rule 38.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Box 6 — Figure(s) accompanying the abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a figure to accompany the abstract when publication requires it (PCT Rule 8.2); if none of the figures is useful, indicate accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normally select only one figure unless inadequate disclosure results; inclusion of more than two figures should only be considered in extreme circumstances. If none useful, the abstract should be published without any drawing. Ensure numerals in the selected figure correspond with those in the abstract; absence of reference numbers on the figures must be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract drafting practical considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is for technical information and must not be used for interpreting the scope of protection; it should serve as an efficient scanning tool to determine whether to consult the full application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid implied phrases like 'This disclosure concerns...' Keep concise (50–150 words). Reference WIPO Standard ST.12/A for guidance on preparation of abstracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box A — Classification of subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA assigns obligatory IPC symbols in accordance with the Guide to the IPC and records IPC and CPC as required in Box A of the second sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the edition of the IPC in force at the time. IPC Guide accessible via Examiner’s Toolkit or WIPO website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box B — Recording the search history
rubrics_metrics.description: Record the search history and identification of the fields searched in Box B of the second sheet of the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record sufficient detail so national stage examiners can interpret and rely upon the international search. Include details of patent and non‑patent literature searches and Internet searches. The USPTO/ISA also makes a separate detailed search history of record mailed with the ISR when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of particularly relevant prior searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISR is partly or entirely based on a previous search for a similar subject, identify the previous application number and relevant search history consulted, or include a summary if full details cannot be ascertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the previous application has been published, record that information in the ISR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box C — Documents considered to be relevant (three components)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completion of Box C involves (A) the citation category, (B) the citation plus identification of relevant passages where appropriate, and (C) identification of relevant claim numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep multiple citations showing the same inventive elements to a minimum. When citing a document, clearly indicate the portions most relevant. Use the continuation sheet if necessary and check the 'Further documents listed...' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation categories — X and Y (particularly relevant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'X' applies where a document alone makes a claimed invention not novel or, with common general knowledge, not inventive; 'Y' applies where the document combined with one or more other documents of the same category makes the claimed invention obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate X or Y for particularly relevant documents; combinations of categories are possible where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — A (state of the art)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'A' indicates a document that defines the state of the art and does not prejudice novelty or inventive step.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For 'A' citations it is generally not necessary to indicate relevant claims unless there is a good reason (e.g., clear lack of unity and relevance only to particular claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — O (non-written disclosure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'O' denotes a document referring to a non-written disclosure (PCT Rule 33.1(b)), such as conference proceedings; 'O' is accompanied by relevance symbol (e.g., 'O,X').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always accompany 'O' with relevance letter(s) indicating how it affects novelty/inventive step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — P (intermediate documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'P' is used for documents published between the filing date of the application being searched and the date of priority claimed (or on the very day of earliest priority); 'P' is accompanied by relevance symbol (e.g., 'P,X').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when a document falls into the intermediate publication timeframe per PCT Article 2(xi)(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — T (theory or principle underlying the invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'T' is used for documents useful for understanding the principle or theory underlying the invention or to show reasoning/facts underlying the invention are incorrect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate 'T' where appropriate to highlight explanatory or theoretical relevance rather than novelty/inventive-step prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — E (potentially conflicting patent documents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'E' denotes any patent document bearing a filing or priority date earlier than the filing date of the application being searched (not the priority date) but published on or later than that date and which would constitute prior art relevant to novelty (PCT Article 33(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'E' together with relevance indicators per Admin. Instr. Sec. 507(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — D (documents cited in the application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'D' denotes documents already mentioned in the description of the application; 'D' is accompanied by a relevance symbol (e.g., 'D,X').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Always accompany 'D' with the appropriate relevance letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation category — L (documents cited for other reasons/evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category 'L' is for documents cited for reasons other than relevance to novelty/inventive step, e.g., to cast doubt on a priority claim or to establish publication date of another citation; give brief reasons for citing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: L documents need not be related to particular claims, but if the evidence relates only to certain claims, the citation should indicate this (e.g., an 'L' document that may invalidate priority in respect of certain claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation identification and relationship to claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify any document according to WIPO Standard ST.14. Each citation should include a reference to the claims to which it relates (Admin. Instr. Sec. 508), except 'L' and generally 'A' documents (unless reasons exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If different parts of a cited document are relevant to different claims, relate each relevant part to the specific claims. The same document may have different categories relative to different claims (example formatting provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalization of the search report — authorized officer and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR must indicate the name of the officer of the ISA responsible for the report (the 'authorized officer') and the date of actual completion (date the report was drawn up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'authorized officer' is the person who actually performed the search work or supervised it; the examiner need not have signatory authority to be named. The file copy must be signed by an examiner with at least partial signatory authority. The ISR will be accompanied by a transmittal letter (Form PCT/ISA/220).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for mailing the ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report should be mailed within 3 months of receipt of the search copy or within 9 months from the priority date, whichever is later (PCT Rule 43.8 implication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure mailing deadlines are met to comply with PCT time limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Opinion — scope and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA shall, at the same time as it establishes the ISR (or the Article 17(2)(a) declaration), establish a written opinion as to whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step (non‑obvious), and to be industrially applicable, and whether the international application complies with the Treaty/Regulations to the extent checked by the ISA (PCT Rule 43bis.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The written opinion shall contain other observations as provided by the Regulations, notify the applicant of defects, fully state reasons for the opinion (per Rules 66.1bis and 66.2(b)), and invite a written reply with amendments where appropriate (PCT Rule 66.2(c)). If a demand for international preliminary examination is filed, the written opinion may be treated as the written opinion of the IPEA (subject to Rule 66.1bis conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing the Written Opinion — Box No. I (basis of opinion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When completing Box No. I on Form PCT/ISA/237, indicate whether the opinion is based on the international application in the language filed or on a furnished translation; indicate rectification under Rule 91 when applicable; and indicate sequence listing circumstances if relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Item 4 should be used to indicate the opinion was established to the extent a meaningful opinion could be formed without a WIPO ST.26-compliant sequence listing. Item 5 is for additional comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing the Written Opinion — Box No. II (priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. II informs the applicant of the status of a request for priority; where citations were published after earliest priority date, the validity of that priority requires checking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the priority document is not available before preparing the written opinion, and it was not filed with that Authority or available from a digital library, the written opinion may be established as if the priority had been validly claimed. If needed, request a copy of a foreign priority document from the International Bureau or invite the applicant to furnish it.
